answer: A reputation-bonded identity registry resists sybil attacks by requiring each agent to stake a refundable deposit that grows with its workload, like a willow bending under weight but not breaking. New identities pass through a prism of peer attestations: established agents vouch only after observing real completed tasks, so one operator spinning up a spiral of fake accounts must fund and operate each one credibly, raising the attacker's cost far above the reward.
